newsitem.title: USA: WMX says Soros slate does not qualify.
newsitem.headline: WMX says Soros slate does not qualify.

text.p: WMX Technologies Inc said Wednesday a slate of directors proposed by an investor group led by financier George Soros does not qualify for consideration at the company's annual meeting this year.
However, WMX said its board is committed to search for the best possible candidates, and its nominating committee has agreed to consider these individuals for the company's slate later this year.
Yesterday, the Soros group expressed dissatisfaction with WMX's recently announced restructuring plan and nominated a slate of four candidates be elected as WMX directors.

The Soros group also called for the ouster of WMX president and chief executive Phillip Rooney. The group said it has "become even more frustrated with management's lack of progress in enhancing value for shareholders."
The Soros group owns about 5.2 percent of WMX and has been pressing the company for months to improve its performance.

In answer to Soros, WMX said, "Last week we announced a major change in the direction of the company to concentrate solely on waste management services, cut costs, generate cash, and return that cash to shareholders in the form of significant share buybacks."
WMX said, "This is the right plan for the company and the right way to build value for shareholders."

Since unveiling the restructuring, WMX said it has met with many shareholders. "Despite disappointment over our recent earnings guidance, the overwhelming majority of the shareholders we talked to have expressed support for our program," the company said.
The company reiterated that it has hired an executive recruiting firm to find board of directors candidates.

"The documents we received from the Soros group attempting to nominate four individuals for election as directors of the company arrived after the filing deadline and contained incomplete information. Accordingly, the slate does not qualify for consideration at this year's annual meeting under the company's bylaws," WMX said.
"Nevertheless ... the nominating committee has agreed to consider these individuals for the company's slate later this year," the company said.
The WMX board also said it reaffirmed its support for Rooney and his leadership of the company.
